commits.message:
fix(coverage): single-source tsconfig + diagnostic precondition

Two findings from round 3:

A. Verifier never checked TS diagnostics. If getSymbolAtLocation
   returned undefined because of an upstream TS error (broken import,
   missing type), collectReferencedOrigins would silently skip the
   binding and record it as uncovered — a false-uncovered failure mode
   masquerading as a missing demo. [LAW:no-silent-fallbacks].

   Added assertProgramClean(program) that runs ts.getPreEmitDiagnostics,
   filters out node_modules, and throws the formatted diagnostic list.
   Behavior verified: a planted 'export const _PROBE: number = "x"'
   in src/index.ts triggers the precondition failure with a precise
   file:line. Removing it returns the suite to clean.

B. Hand-listed compiler options drifted from tsconfig.json in subtle
   ways. Programmatic lib: ['ES2022'] does not pull in the same
   ambient declarations as tsconfig's ["ES2022"] — Object.hasOwn was
   unrecognized, and the diagnostic pass flagged real source code as
   broken. [LAW:one-source-of-truth].

   loadCompilerOptions() now reads tsconfig.json via ts.readConfigFile
   + ts.parseJsonConfigFileContent, so the verifier's type-system view
   IS the build's view. Surgical local overrides: noEmit (we never
   emit), drop rootDir/outDir (our rootNames span src/ + examples/
   while tsconfig restricts to src/), turn off noUnused* (irrelevant
   to symbol resolution and would flag legitimate example patterns),
   merge 'node' into types (both halves touch Node builtins).

Pushed back on round-3 finding C (SHA-pin third-party action) and
resolved with reasoning: the action is first-party (same owner), the
vendor's own README recommends @v1, and the action doesn't ship
immutable semver tags. The threat model SHA-pinning addresses doesn't
apply.

fix(coverage): canonical lib name, single examples walk, accurate allowlist comment

Three more findings from Copilot's second pass:

A. extract.ts: lib option uses canonical name 'ES2022' (matching
   tsconfig.json) instead of 'lib.es2022.d.ts'. The d.ts-filename form
   bypasses TS's lib-name resolution path; the name form is what the
   compiler processes through parseCompilerOptions.

B. extract.ts + coverage.test.ts: examples/ is now walked exactly once.
   makeProgram() returns the exampleFiles list it actually constructed
   the program from, and the test consumes that list directly for
   collectReferencedOrigins. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] — two walks of
   the same tree are two derivations of the same logical set, and
   could in principle diverge. One walk, one set, two consumers.

C. coverage-allowlist.ts: comment no longer lies about ordering. The
   entries are grouped by flagship and alphabetical within each group;
   the comment now says that. [LAW:comments-explain-why-only] — the
   correct version also explains why (contiguous block deletion when
   a flagship lands its demos).

fix(coverage,deploy): address PR-32 review findings

Six findings from Copilot, all valid:

1. extract.ts: ENTRY_MODULES is now derived from package.json#exports
   at test-load time, not a hand-list. The dist→src mapping inverts the
   tsc rootDir/outDir convention; each derived source path is asserted
   to exist on disk so a misconfigured exports entry fails the verifier
   load loudly. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] now honored by the
   implementation as well as the comment.

2. extract.ts: types: ['node'] (not []) so Node-builtin references in
   src/ and examples/ resolve through the proper @types/node ambient
   declarations rather than degrading to any. Not coupled to
   tsconfig.demo.json — coupling would make the verifier brittle to
   unrelated build-config changes.

3. extract.ts: isUnderSrc() uses path.relative + isAbsolute/startsWith('..')
   instead of raw-string startsWith. Robust to OS path separator and
   symlink/realpath differences.

4. coverage.test.ts: fix redundant.push indentation to match the
   enclosing if-block body.

5. coverage.test.ts: formatGap renders origin.file relative to
   REPO_ROOT — portable error output, not tied to checkout path.

6. deploy.yml: skip deploy job on fork PRs. GitHub forces GITHUB_TOKEN
   to read-only for fork pull_request events (correctly), so the
   gh-pages push and sticky-comment write would otherwise fail noisily.
   The if-condition lives at the exact trust boundary
   (head.repo.full_name == github.repository). Fork PRs still run
   ci.yml; preview-for-fork-PRs requires the workflow_run two-stage
   pattern, deferred.

All checks: vitest green (8867 pass / 7 skip), tsc clean, yaml valid.

ci(deploy): docs via gh-pages-multiplexer (master + PR previews)

Replace the single-deployment actions/deploy-pages workflow with the
gh-pages-multiplexer action. This deploys to versioned subdirectories
on the gh-pages branch, generates an index page, injects a nav widget,
and posts sticky PR preview comments.

Triggers: push to master AND every pull_request — same job, same
steps; the only variance is the version slot value (`master` for
master pushes, `pr-<N>` for PRs).

Path A integration per the action's install guide: VitePress already
reads process.env.VITEPRESS_BASE in docs/.vitepress/config.ts, so the
build emits absolute URLs rooted at the deploy slot at build time and
the action runs with base-path-mode: none (no post-hoc rewriting).

The slot value (`steps.version.outputs.slot`) is the single source
of truth read by both the VITEPRESS_BASE env var and the action's
`version:` input — drift between them would 404 every deep asset.

Verified locally with VITEPRESS_BASE=/rich-js/pr-32/: every href and
src in the built dist resolves under that path with no <base> tag.

After this lands, the repo's Pages source must be flipped from
'workflow' to 'branch / gh-pages' for the multiplexer's pushes to be
served. The branch will be created by the first successful run.

[LAW:single-enforcer] One workflow owns deployment; ci.yml continues
to own validation. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] slot value is computed
once, consumed twice. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] the workflow
steps run unconditionally; the slot value carries the variance.

test(coverage): API→demo coverage verifier (rich-demos-l2x.1)

Turn 'every public export is demonstrated in examples/' into a machine
check, keystone of epic rich-demos-l2x.

The verifier compiles src/ + examples/ as one TypeScript program and
uses the type checker to resolve symbols across the boundary. Public
exports are derived from getExportsOfModule() on the four entry
modules in package.json's exports field — never a hand-maintained
list. References in examples/ are resolved through SymbolFlags.Alias
chains back to the same declaration sites, so deep imports cover the
barrel export for the same underlying symbol.

The allowlist (test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts) is the explicit
escape hatch: every entry is either *burndown* (tagged with the
flagship demo that will own coverage) or *permanent* (justified). The
test enforces three invariants over (universe, references, allowlist):

  1. Every uncovered export is allowlisted with a justification.
  2. Every allowlist entry points to a real public export.
  3. No allowlist entry is already covered by a demo.

Invariants 2 and 3 prevent the allowlist itself from becoming a silent
fallback — dead entries fail loudly, redundant entries fail loudly.

Seeded the burndown list (~100 entries) from today's uncovered set,
each tagged with the flagship that will absorb it (themes-and-color-
studio, renderables-gallery, widgets-playground, markup-and-text-lab,
live-progress-console). Flagship-build tickets remove their entries
as coverage lands.

Behavior verified by injecting each of the three failure cases and
observing the precise error message.

[LAW:verifiable-goals] 'All public functionality is demoed' is now a
build that fails when a new export has no demo. [LAW:one-source-of-
truth] The public-export set comes from the entry modules; no hand-
maintained list. [LAW:no-silent-fallbacks] Three orthogonal invariants
prevent allowlist drift.

Refs: rich-demos-l2x.1
